plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Static gain magnitude and response lag, which determine what u can move y toward 0.6 and how fast a controller can act.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain hypothesis is right, y rises from ~0.38 by ~0.05-0.15 over 10s after 1-3s lag, with noise ~+/-0.02, staying well below 0.85.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and steady-state u to reach 0.6, which E1 weakened by showing u=0.4 cannot hold 0.3; a second higher amplitude separates pump gain from drain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain hypothesis is right, y will stop falling and rise from ~0.28 by ~0.05-0.15 over 8s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.50, distinguishing drain-dominated fall at u=0.4 from pump-driven rise.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether higher u reverses the E1 fall and produces net rise (gain magnitude and steady-state u for 0.6), which determines if target is reachable and what feedforward u to use.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain hypothesis is right, the E1 fall will arrest within 2-3 s then y rises from ~0.28 by ~0.05-0.12 to ~0.33-0.40 over 8 s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.50; continued fall would falsify H1.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Natural drain rate and time constant at u=0, which separates pump gain from drain and determines feedforward u and integral needed to hold 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If fast-drain hypothesis is right, y falls from ~0.39 exponentially to ~0.08-0.18 over 10 s, initial slope ~-0.05 to -0.07/s slowing as level drops, noise +/-0.01; slow fall would falsify H4.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether higher u sustains stronger rise and what feedforward holds 0.6, separating linear gain from saturation and determining reachable target.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain hypothesis is right, y will arrest fall within ~2-3 s then rise from ~0.21 by ~0.08-0.15 to ~0.29-0.36 over 8 s at ~0.01-0.02/s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.45; continued fall would falsify H1.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Linearity of gain and steady-state u to hold 0.6, which determines feedforward and whether target is reachable without saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain and fast-drain hypotheses are right, y holds near 0.32 for ~1.5-2.5 s lag then rises at ~0.015-0.025/s to ~0.40-0.46 over 6 s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.55; continued fall or flat would falsify H1 and imply saturation or higher drain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u~0.7 still produces net rise at y~0.5 and at what rate, separating high-level drain from pump gain to pin down feedforward u for 0.6 and test linearity near target.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain and fast-drain hypotheses are right, y holds ~0.50-0.52 for ~1-2 s lag then rises at ~0.015-0.030/s by ~0.04-0.08 to ~0.55-0.59 over 4 s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.65; flat or fall would falsify H1/H6 and imply stronger high-level drain or saturation.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state pump duty to hold y=0.6 (H6) and linearity near target (H5), which set feedforward and prevent offset or overshoot in the controller.
experiments.expected_observation: If revised H1/H6 is right (u=0.7 equilibrium above 0.6), y will hold ~0.60-0.62 for ~1-2 s lag then stay flat or fall slowly at -0.005 to -0.02/s by 0.02-0.04 to ~0.57-0.60 over 4 s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.65; continued rise would falsify H6 and imply much higher equilibrium.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state pump duty to hold y=0.6 (H6), which sets feedforward and prevents offset; u=0.4 from high level brackets E8 rise at u=0.55.
experiments.expected_observation: If revised H6 is right (hold u for 0.6 is 0.45-0.53), y will hold ~0.64-0.65 for 1-2 s lag then fall at ~0.005-0.02/s by ~0.02-0.06 to ~0.59-0.63 over 4 s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.67; continued rise would falsify H6 and imply hold u below 0.4.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state pump duty to hold y=0.6 (H6), which sets feedforward and prevents offset; u=0.48 midpoints E8 rise at 0.55 and E9 slight fall at 0.40.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H6 is right (hold u for 0.6 is ~0.45-0.50), y will hold ~0.63 for 1-2 s lag then stay flat within 0.61-0.65, drift <+/-0.01/s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.70; clear rise would imply hold <0.45, clear fall would imply hold >0.50.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state pump duty to hold y=0.6 (H6), which sets feedforward and prevents offset; u=0.52 bisects E8 rise at 0.55 and E10 fall at 0.48.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H6 is right (hold u ~0.50-0.54), y will stay ~0.60-0.62 for 0.5-1.5 s lag then drift <+/-0.01/s to 0.59-0.63 over 4 s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.66; clear rise >0.03 would imply hold <0.50, clear fall >0.03 would imply hold >0.54.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state pump duty to hold y=0.6 (H6), which sets feedforward and prevents offset; u=0.535 bisects E8 rise at 0.55 and E11 slight fall at 0.52.
experiments.expected_observation: If H1/H6 is right (hold u ~0.52-0.55), y will hold ~0.59 for 0.5-1.5 s lag then stay flat 0.58-0.61, drift <+/-0.01/s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.65; clear rise >0.03 would imply hold <0.52, clear fall >0.03 would imply hold >0.55.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Response delay and approach rate (C3 slower response vs C1/C2 gain/drain), which determines whether controller needs detuning for delay or higher feedforward for gain/drain.
experiments.expected_observation: If slower-response hypothesis C3 is right, y will stay ~0.13-0.16 flat for ~6-10 s after step, then begin rising to ~0.25-0.40 by 12 s with noise +/-0.015, staying below 0.50. Prompt rise within 1-3 s would falsify C3 and favor weaker-actuator or outflow change.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Post-delay approach rate and static gain after the long delay (C1 weaker actuator vs C3 slower response), which sets feedforward u and controller gain to reach 0.6 without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If C3 slower-response is right and the E13 delay has largely elapsed, y will rise promptly from ~0.14 at ~0.01-0.02/s to ~0.26-0.36 over 12s with noise +/-0.01, staying below 0.45. Flat stay <0.20 would favor C1 weaker actuator; continued fall would favor C2 faster outflow.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Natural drain rate and delayed fall timing at u=0 (C2 vs C3), which separates faster outflow from pure delay and sets feedforward and integral detuning to hold 0.6 without oscillation.
experiments.expected_observation: If C3 slower-response is right, y will hold near 0.52 flat for ~7-9 s after step to 0, then begin falling at ~0.015-0.03/s to ~0.35-0.47 by 15 s with noise +/-0.01, staying above 0.30. Prompt fall within 1-3 s to below 0.35 would favor C2 faster outflow and falsify pure delay.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Delay before u=0 fall begins and post-delay drain rate, which separates pure long delay from loss of drain and sets integral detuning and feedforward needed to hold 0.6 without oscillation.
experiments.expected_observation: If C3 slower-response is right, y will hold near 0.58-0.60 flat within +/-0.02 for the first ~5-10 s after step to 0, then begin falling at ~0.015-0.03/s to ~0.35-0.50 by 20 s with noise +/-0.015, staying above 0.30. Prompt fall within 1-3 s would falsify C3 and favor residual drain dynamics; continued flat with no fall for full 20 s would imply delay >30 s total including E15 or much slower approach.

ledger.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases dy/dt and level y (positive static gain).
Step response has short lag of 0.5-2 s before trend changes after u change, shorter for small steps near target.
There is negligible dead-zone; u>=0.4 produces rise relative to u=0, but u<0.4 untested.
At u=0 the level decays on its own toward low values with time constant of order 11-16 s.
Gain is approximately linear across u in [0,0.8] and y up to 0.65 with no strong saturation.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.6 is ~0.52-0.55; u=0.55 rises at 0.60-0.64, u=0.52 is ~flat/slight fall, u=0.48 falls.
Sensor noise is small (+/-0.015) relative to control band width 0.10.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller rise rate and lower held level with similar short lag.
Change is faster outflow: faster fall at u=0 and lower level held by same u with similar short lag.
Change is slower response: longer delay ~8-15+s before trend changes and slower approach, causing flat holds then delayed rise/fall and oscillation under old controller.
Change is sensor offset or noise change: different bias or larger variance rather than dynamics change.
